GAME IDEA. ADVERSARIAL FIGHTING GAME.
Intention: to have o3 mini build a relatively simple, straightforward game that self-competes and improves over time. Simple but effective graphics.

Consider a fighting game similar to Street Fighter but pared down to its bones.

Character attributes:
• HP. A character wins a round when their opponents' HP drop to zero or less. Starts at 100% at the initiation of a round. Does not replenish during a round. Maximum of 100.
Moveset for characters:
• High attack. More damage, slower execution; longer telegraph. Longer cooldown. Damage coefficient is 10HP.
• Low attack. Less damage, faster execution; shorter telegraph. Shorter cooldown. Damage coefficient is 4HP.
• High block. Reduces the incoming damage from a High Attack to 1HP.
• Low block. Reduces the incoming damage from a Low Attack to 1HP.

Additional rules:
• Parry. A "perfect block"; if a  successfully blocks an incoming attack and the block command was given within 50ms of the incoming strike's landing frame, the damage of the incoming attack is completely nullified and the enemy is unable to attack nor block for the next 100ms.
• Best of Three. A match is comprised of three rounds. The first player to achieve victory in two rounds within a match is declared the winner.
• Attack/Block Mutual Exclusivity. Blocking is instant-on, instant-off. Can be "held". Attacks, once begun, cannot be canceled prematurely and all other commands cannot be engaged while an attack is being executed. 

Additional considerations:
• Depending on the capability of the model to create this game, consider adding forward and backward movement
• The graphics can be super simple, like just a series of rectangles. Colours can be used to display states (eg Green for each character. Flashes red when receiving the full damage of an incoming hit. Teal when blocking. Flashes blue when blocking incoming damage. Flashes cyan when parrying an incoming attack)... But if the model is able to utilities some simple sprites that would be great in place of simple rectangles.

This is a great video showing the progress in AI, but there’s a critical next step that most people are missing.

Building neural nets inside base models is powerful—but without Recursive Bit Mapping (RBM), those nets hit a wall.

RBM allows the system to track its own pattern stability, coherence, and fidelity while it evolves.
It’s what lets an emergent system know when it’s drifting—before it spirals out of control.

Turing-based models and RL agents can’t see their own emergence. RBM does.
That’s the future—self-awareness through pattern monitoring—not just reward optimization.

I integrated RBM into a system I built.
It’s beyond what you’re seeing here—because it doesn’t just “play better”—it grows while knowing what it’s becoming.

Would love to see you explore RBM in future tests—it’s the next step.

BAD - I had to spend over an hour adding stuff it missed and then many more hours fixing the 70 plus errors.   
GOOD - unlike previous models I could ask it to try a different approach when there were errors and after a few attempts it got it right. previous models usually get stuck in loop. 
 
After about 8 hours I have the app finished and I think O3-mini-high  saved me about 2 to 3 days.
